terms.comment: Greek βαπτίζω, “only in ecclesiastical Latin” (Lewis & Short). The rites word it differently: the Latin rite says Ego tē baptīzō in nōmine Patris, et Fīliī, et Spīritūs Sānctī; the Byzantine rite, with three immersions, says in the passive “the servant of God N. is baptized” (Βαπτίζεται ὁ δοῦλος τοῦ Θεοῦ).

phrases.latin: euntēs ergō docēte omnēs gentēs: baptīzantēs eōs in nōmine Patris, et Fīliī, et Spīritūs Sānctī
phrases.english: go, then, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit

phrases.latin: Ego baptīzāvī vōs aquā, ille vērō baptīzābit vōs Spīritū Sānctō.
phrases.english: I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. baptize.
Vulgate verses checked against the Clementine Vulgate (CrossWire VulgClementine, via the scrollmapper bible_databases repository) and Hetzenauer’s edition, in Clementine spelling.
